utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. Yes, I can follow the proceedings in my own language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Oric, and good morning to you as well. You may be seated. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. Also good morning to my learned friends of the Defence. I'm here together with Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, Ms. Joanne Richardson, and our case manager, Mrs. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben, and good morning to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. My name is Vasvija Vidovic, and together with Mr. John Jones I appear for Mr. Oric. With us today are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic. In the course of the day we shall also be joined by other members of our team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Ms. Vidovic, and good morning to you and your team as well. Are you feeling well?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hear -- yes. We've got two options: We can thrash any preliminaries now, all or some of them, if there are several; or we can start with the witness straight away and finish with him. I take it that you're both trying to finish with him today, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in my estimation, as far as I'm concerned, at least, as I will be doing the examination-in-chief, it will be a rather short testimony, unless there are technical problems. I think it should be over in about an hour. I have told my colleagues from the Prosecution this. We would be very happy if Mr. Bilic could begin today and finish as soon as possible because he has other obligations that cannot delayed next week at the end of the week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We would be very happy if we could do that. Who will be examining the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I will do so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you anticipate to have a short cross-examination as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: When it is Mr. Bilic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. It will be Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Unless there are some urgent matters that you would like to raise in a preliminary way, I suggest that we start with the witness and finish with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I have a submission to make regarding the Trial Chamber expert, but that can wait.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Okay. So do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Usher. In the meantime, just to inform you, I hope to be able to sign, during the break, the decision on your motion on Rule -- on Colonel Fenzel or whatever his name is. And I take this opportunity to thank the Prosecution for having come forward with their response yesterday, which made it possible for us to work on it and come to a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Monday we are working in the afternoon. Please do remember that. This witness doesn't have any protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I will be speaking in English, and my words are being simultaneously translated to you in your own language so as to make it possible for you to follow what is being said here. If there are at any moment, at any time, problems with the reception of interpretation, please draw my attention straight away. So on behalf of the Tribunal, I should like to welcome you as a Defence witness. I'm the Presiding Judge. My name is Carmel Agius. I come from Malta. To my right I am flanked by Judge Hans Hendrik Brydensholt from the Kingdom of Denmark, and to my left, Judge Professor Albin Eser from the Republic of Germany. This is a case against Naser Oric, and you are one of the Defence witnesses. Very soon you will start with your testimony, but before you can do so our Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, equivalent to an oath in several jurisdictions, to the effect that in the course of your testimony you undertake to testify the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is going to be handed to you now by Madam Usher. Please take it in your hands, read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us, that you will be testifying the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And come as near as you can to the microphones. Don't stay too far away from them because otherwise we'll have problems. What's going to happen is Ms. Vidovic, who is lead counsel for Naser Oric in this case, will be examining you in chief, and she will then be followed by Mr. Di Fazio for the Prosecution on cross-examination. And we hope to be able to send you back home very soon. For that to be possible, we need your cooperation, and your cooperation consists not only in testifying the truth but in keeping your answers as concise and as precise as follows. Please don't give us more information than you are asked for. Answer the questions that are put to you, whichever -- wherever they are coming from. Answer each question truthfully, but answer the question, the whole question, and nothing but the question. Thank you. Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Guster.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you and I speak the same language - and I've already explained this to you during the proofing - I wish to ask you to always pause for a moment after I put my question so that the interpreters can interpret my question. Do you understand this?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell Their Honours your full first and last name.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Ejub Guster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're a Bosniak Muslim?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were born on the 18th of January, 1964, in Cerska in the hamlet of Gusteri?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your father's name is Ibran and your mother's name Hasna, nee Avdic?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are married and you are the father of six?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By occupation you are in charge of machinery -- a machine operator in a mine?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You completed primary school in Cerska in 1978?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you completed secondary school in Vlasenica in 1982?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On completion of secondary school, you worked in various building construction companies in Belgrade until 1991 when you lost your job in the company called Ivan Milutinovic in Belgrade where you were made redundant?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You served your military service in Pazen in the Republic of Croatia in 1983, and in 1984 you were in the infantry, and after that you were a dog handler?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While working in Belgrade, you spent nearly every weekend in your village of Gusteri?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Travelling from Belgrade to Gusteri and back you had occasion to meet other people hailing from Podrinje and working in Belgrade in that time period?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1988, did you meet Mr. Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We were introduced by some friends of mine from Cerska, who knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was Mr. Naser Oric doing at the time, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: He was working as a policeman in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to see him more than once before the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. In the course of 1998 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's apology, 1988.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and 1989, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean you knew him well?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have a feeling that you need to pause a little bit between question and answer. I can feel the tension in the interpreters' booths. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, please pause just a little bit after my question so that the question can be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether this means that you knew Mr. Oric well.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: When the war broke out, I was in Cerska, in my hamlet of Gusteri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember - and tell us very briefly - how the defence of your hamlet of Gusteri was organised.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: There was an armed group of men defending it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was at the head of that group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Meho Velic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many men were in the group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About 20 men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: They were armed with hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally belong to that armed group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No, I didn't have a weapon. In agreement with the other villagers, with the other villagers and two other men -- with two other men, I collected food for the refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you collect that food?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We went into the woods to find fruits in the forest; mushrooms, strawberries, anything else, berries; then we planted potatoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many refugees were there in your village in the course of 1992 before the fall of your hamlet?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About a thousand refugees. There were about a thousand in my little hamlet of Gusteri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people in the course of 1992 stayed in your own house?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About 30 people stayed in my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. On the 26th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How? In what way? How were you wounded?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I was on my way to dig potatoes in the area between us and the Serbs, and I stepped on a land-mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What injuries did you sustain on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: My heel and my lower leg were damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Cerska could you get any kind of medical assistance?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. There was no doctor, only a medical technician who didn't have enough medicines or material.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the beginning of 1993, did you manage to have your wound heal?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when, in your opinion, the situation in Cerska grew much worse?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Towards the end of November 1992, the Serbs were attacking Cerska intensively, more and more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of attacks were these?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Infantry, artillery, and air attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What consequences did this have for the local population?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: In my village, many people were killed and many people were wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened towards the end of January 1993 in Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: The situation was very tense. Hamlet after hamlet started to fall: Velici, Hodjici, Grbici, Ferhatovici, and finally my own hamlet of Gusteri. These were all hamlets of Cerska.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the Chamber would find it helpful, we can have map D814 put on the ELMO so that the witness can show where his hamlet is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the proofing, you told me that none of the maps that we had contained the village. Your Honours, however, the witness is able to find and pinpoint the village on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you pinpoint the village on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I can't read the letters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please take a look at the map itself.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: By your leave, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please turn to your right, to the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. Velici, Hodjici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can the technicians focus on that part of the map. I think, Madam Usher, you need to put it further down, and then we zoom in. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Velici, Hodjici, Grbici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ferhatovici, and my village, Gusteri.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, the witness indicates various spots along the line drawn on the map between Velici and Hakalasi and between Jasikovice and Mustajbasici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The map can be returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, when did your village of Gusteri fall?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: On the 3rd of February, 1993, the Serbs launched intense attacks against the village of Gusteri.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, was your house in fact hit and destroyed?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. On that occasion three shells landed on my own home, and in the process my 5-year-old daughter was wounded, as were two more children who were in my house. None of the children were older than 14. With the children there, there were many refugees who were staying at my house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wounded as well?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do after the attack?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I left the house on the 3rd of February, 1993, because I practically had nowhere to stay. I set out on foot along the river.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you set out with? Who was with you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: My wife, who was pregnant, and in her arms she was carrying my wounded child. Even though it was wintertime, I was wearing only a shirt because I did not manage to take anything else. The attack was a very fierce one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What direction were you headed?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I set out with a mass of people in the direction of Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This massive group of people that you set out with toward Konjevic Polje, was it able to proceed in peace?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. There was intense shelling. Shells were landing, people were getting killed, the children were screaming; there were many wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in spite of that, manage to reach Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I did. We were received by a family by the name of Ramici in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people went over to Konjevic Polje from the area of Cerska?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Thousands of people -- well, I say "thousands of people." There were many. I don't know the exact numbers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About a month.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is the house of the Ramic family in Konjevic Polje located?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: It was about 100 metres away from the school there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you had arrived in Konjevic Polje, did the Serb forces start exerting pressure on Konjevic Polje as well?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. There were intense attacks from the direction of Zvornik and Bilici [as interpreted] because one knew that Konjevic Polje was going to fall imminently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or rather, Your Honour, I wish to enter a correction for the record. The witness said: "From the direction of Zvornik and Milici," not Bilici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic. Do you agree, Mr. Guster?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether representatives of UNPROFOR forces came to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, on the 6th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you recall of the events taking place on the 6th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes: Throngs of people gathered around the school which was near to the house where I was staying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, go on.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: The people who gathered there realised that the fall of Konjevic Polje was imminent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people there, including yourself, were you hoping that somebody was going to assist you, help you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We were hoping that the UNPROFOR was going to help us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this time, Your Honour, I would like a video-clip to be played, P427, a Prosecution exhibit, one out of two videos, 3284, point started at 00.30.32, ending at 00.30.49.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, do you recall these scenes? Have you witnessed them?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This happened on the 6th of March, 1993 in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you among the people here?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I was some 10 to 15 metres away from this point among the people gathered who can be seen here in this frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the man with grey hair on this video?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That's General Morillon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him that day there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, he was there on that day, in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take a good look at him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the person who General Morillon is talking to?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's my neighbour, Tauric, who used to work in Switzerland before the war. Talovic, he spoke French well. That's why he's talking to General Morillon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the video-clip to be played further, up to 31.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone on this still?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Mr. Oric. In the yellow -- with the yellow hood. He was in Konjevic Polje on that day. That's the man with the yellow hood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You told us that you knew Mr. Oric before the war. Did you know anything about his role when you saw him there -- or rather, let me ask you this first: Did you see Oric in this mass of people on that day?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. He is the man, the man with the yellow hood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. At the time, were you familiar with his -- with the role that he played in this time period?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody from among the people there speak to you about Oric or about his role or his activities at the time?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. The people were only concerned with their own safety. Nobody was interested in these matters at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the clip be played further, until 32.03, and stop there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing this person that day?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. He is a Muslim from Srebrenica who was there, interpreting for the UNPROFOR members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave Konjevic Polje together with your family?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I did; on the 9th of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your journey to Konjevic Polje -- or rather, what was your journey from Konjevic Polje to Srebrenica like?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I set out on the journey with a large group of people; men, women, and children. On the way, many shells landed on these large numbers of civilians. There was artillery from the direction of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name of the location.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name of the location from which the shellings -- the shells you mentioned earlier were fired.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: From Tumace. The shelling came from the direction of Tumace.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Do you recall the events happening in Hrncic Polje, or rather, did you pass through Hrncic Polje?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. On the 9th of March, 1993, when I reached Hrncic Polje, there was a shell hitting a large group of people, some 100 of them were killed. My cousin Mejra Uvalic, her head was blown up by the shell that landed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are terrible scenes that this Trial Chamber has to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps I should refrain from putting such questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you talking about Mejra or the child?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Mejra was holding a child in her arms, and it was the child's head that was blown up by the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, can you continue?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. One moment. Sorry -- I apologise to you, Ms. Vidovic, for interrupting you. But I am informed that the witness was asking for a break and that somehow this was not brought to our attention. Do you need a short break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can continue. I have overcome the moment. Because these scenes that I experienced -- this was just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, I will no longer inquire after these matters. I wish to ask you the following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you finally arrive in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: On the 9th of March, 1993, I arrived in Srebrenica with my family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you find accommodation, if any?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We stayed outdoors, out in the street. Although it was wintertime, I was wearing only a shirt. I remember that we found some old disused car tires that we set fire to to -- for heating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend outdoors with your family?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About five days.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we play a video-clip at this time, number 3671, which we received from Prosecution with receipt number 266A, from 00.56.46 up until 00.56.3 -- 56. So please stop at 00.56.56.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, do you know what is shown in this video?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This is the cemetery in Srebrenica. These -- the people were -- who were on their way from Konjevic Polje to Srebrenica and got killed in the process were buried here. There were women and children among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the cemetery where you buried people who got killed on their way from Konjevic Polje to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I've said so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please can we play the video further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, are these the scenes you saw after you arrived in Srebrenica in March 1993?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. These were the scenes that I, myself, saw out in the street, as did the people who were shown on the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this video please be assigned an exhibit number, a Defence exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the next number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D1008, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: D1008. So this video -- the video that you've shown is -- contains more than what we have seen or just the segment that we have seen?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a clip of the video, but the entire video footage contains scenes such as these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. No, but what you are tendering in evidence, in other words, is this part that we have seen and not anything else, not anything beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So this video-clip that we have seen is being tendered in evidence and is being given Exhibit Number D1008. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones -- Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I have no problem at all, of course, with the video going into evidence, but I would like to see it before I cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I haven't seen it. No, not the whole thing. I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it's the whole thing that's being tendered. MR. DI FAZIO: It's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I put the question. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry, then I misunderstood. I've got no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I had the same preoccupation, concern you had. I was asking precisely whether it was a video-recording containing more scenes than what we have seen and more material than what was being tendered or whether it was just what we saw on the screen a few minutes ago, and I'm told that it's only what we saw on the screen that's being tendered. All right? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is why I specified the times from/to for the record, to avoid any confusion, and we have copies prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And that's why I pointed -- I asked the question, actually, because I could anticipate a problem. So, yes, let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, did you manage to find accommodation somewhere in Srebrenica at last?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, on the fifth day I found accommodation in a building. We cleared rubble out of an apartment which did not have windows or doors. I got nylon from a man that I was able to put on the windows, and I found a blanket that I put into the door post. And we -- I found some sheets and bedding so that we didn't have to stay out in the street anymore.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any food or water at the time?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. The water was polluted and I didn't have any food.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you survive?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We ate hazel tree catkin. That's how we managed to get by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this, Mr. Guster, what happened to your family?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: On the 19th of March, 1993, I managed to put my wife, children, and mother-in-law on an UNPROFOR truck that was headed to Tuzla, although my wife was -- was pregnant, she managed to bring my children to Tuzla alive. There were many women and children on the trucks, and their children had difficulties surviving the journey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the children actually suffocated on their way to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That's what my wife told me of her journey from Srebrenica to Tuzla. On the truck with her there was a neighbour, a lady, who had her sons there, and they suffocated simply because of the numbers of people crammed up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you stay behind in Srebrenica after you sent your wife away; and what did you do?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed behind in Srebrenica. I reported to the municipality to help with the evacuation of the wounded. On the 19th of March, 1993, a convoy carrying food came. And on that same day, I went out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After having reported there, did you regularly go to the municipality building?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I spent the entire days there, from early in the morning until late at night, together with the others, waiting for an UNPROFOR APC in order to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you were there on the 21st of March, 1993, or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I was there on the 21st of March, 1993. I was there in front of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what time of day it was when you arrived in front of the municipality building?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I was there at 7.00 in the morning in front of the municipal building, waiting for an UNPROFOR vehicle to evacuate the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall who was with you there?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I was with the people from Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember specifically the names of some of the persons you were with?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. From Kamenica and Konjevic Polje, his nickname was Bujak [as interpreted]. His name Sahin Zahirovic, another person also from Konjevic Polje. We were standing in front of the municipal building, waiting, and discussing what we would do in case the wounded were not evacuated. We thought it wise to set out for Tuzla on foot because we felt that the fall of Srebrenica was imminent. We discussed these issues and stayed there until some time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, I apologise. Can you please repeat the names of the persons because the record shows that you were with the person called Bujak.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. His nickname was Burik. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore Burek?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: B-u-r-e-k?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Not B-u-r-i-k but B-u-r-e-k.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you repeat the name of the other person.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Sakim Zahirovic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: S-a-h-i-n; isn't that right, Mr. Guster?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. An "n" at the end, not an "m."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is very important for us, that's why I insist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please. From the point where you were standing with these men, were you able to see the street leading to the post office in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We could see the length of the street, and there is a clear line of sight all the way to the post office. We could see the UNPROFOR vehicle because the UNPROFOR was based in the PTT.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time on that day when you observed the appearance of a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. It was an UNPROFOR APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time this APC turned up?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. It was at around 10.30. On that day a man from Konjevic Polje was there who had a watch.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could the witness now be shown a photograph. Could the photograph also be placed on the ELMO, please. Could you please lower it a little. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise anyone on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's me, observing the carrying of ill people, patients, into the APC on stretchers. That's me. I was wearing a check shirt and dark trousers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember this scene, Mr. Guster?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very well. This was on the 21st of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this photograph be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Ms. Vidovic. This photograph will become Defence Exhibit D1009.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, you told us that you observed an APC turning up, an UNPROFOR APC, and that it was moving from the direction of the post office toward the centre. Do you remember whether in front of this APC there was another dark luxury vehicle or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. We were watching the APC closely and its movements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you watching the movements of the APC closely?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We wanted to see where it would stop, where it would park, so that we could get as close to it as possible, because I was hoping to get into it myself and be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like a new video-clip to be played now. We will view it in stages.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, please look at the video very carefully. Can you please play it and stop at 0.04.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, please look at the road in front of the vehicle. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you play the video further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the road you were observing on that day, leading from the post office to the municipal building?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That is the street --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- leading from the post office to the municipal building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, we are at 00.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you play on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the road we were talking about? Is it still the same road?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please play on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a good look at this still. Do you know anyone in this still?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. In the bottom left-corner, wearing a white jacket, that's Sahin Zahirovic, from Konjevic Polje, who was with me that morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. For the record, we are at 01.32.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please play on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise anyone now on this still?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. A man from Konjevic Polje whose nickname was Burek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take the pointer and indicate -- is that him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, we are at 01.41, and the witness indicates the first person on the far left of the still. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, will you tell us his name, or nickname, again.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. He's a man from Konjevic Polje, and his nickname was Burek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please play on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise someone now?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That's me, wearing a shirt. I am observing the wounded being carried into the APC on stretchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And please play the video to the end now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we were at still 02.25.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, do you remember the details of the event which we saw on the video-clip?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This was on the 21st of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you tendering this video in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. Of course, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Judge Eser would like to know the provenance -- Judge Brydensholt. So this video has just been played, been tendered by the Defence, and marked as Defence D1010.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we cannot discuss this before the witness right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received it from a source which we don't wish to reveal now. All I can say is that Mr. Birtley saw the entire clip together with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the source is a sensitive one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened after the UNPROFOR vehicle parked?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The vehicle arrived at the municipal building. Across the street from the municipal building is a department store on the left-hand side, and that's where the vehicle parked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened after the vehicle parked?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: The door of the APC opened, and several UNPROFOR soldiers came out. They had UN insignia and they were wearing blue helmets on their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did someone come out of the vehicle who did not have a blue helmet on his head or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Two people in civilian clothes got out. One was filming; the other one had an arm missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: The man wearing civilian clothes who had an arm missing set out with two UNPROFOR men along the street from the municipal building to a private house at the top of the street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far was this house from the place you were standing in?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About 150 metres, not more.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can the witness now be shown paragraph C2. Your Honours, it's already on the screen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a picture on the screen?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you recognise, if anything, on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This is that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indicate it, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This is the house at the top of the street where the armless man with two UNPROFOR men went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So one moment, Ms. Vidovic, please. For the record, the witness points at the house which is shown on the photo between the two buildings on the sides -- on the sides. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what you remember, what happened next, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The man without an arm, who went with two UNPROFOR men, entered the house -- or rather, they came to the entrance to the house, which was at the side of the house. We were watching this. We were looking to see what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. We thought they had gone to collect someone who was wounded or ill. We didn't know what this was about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At some point did you see anyone around the house again?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Some ten minutes later, or maybe even less, a tall man came out. He was wearing a uniform. He came to the corner of the house, and he was waving his hand, indicating to us that he needed help. He was beckoning to us who were near the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "us," will you say who you mean.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes: Me, Sahin, and Burek.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of you go there to help?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, Sahin and Burek went along the street from a spot near the municipal building towards the house. At one point, two UNPROFOR men showed up, and they were leading a sick person who was leaning against them. Sahin and Burek ran up, as did another man. They took over that person from the UNPROFOR men and brought the person to a stretcher. The UNPROFOR soldiers took over the person and put the person on a stretcher and put the stretcher in the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself approach the house?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Sahin did and so did Burek. I was just watching all the time because I had a bad leg. My leg was painful and I couldn't walk. I was trying to get into the APC myself to be evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to show the videotape from 01.26 to 01.33. For purposes of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly we will do that very soon, yes, Ms. Vidovic. Yes, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Before we go back to the video, could we perhaps see once more the last picture, C2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we can. Of course we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: The picture -- the photo of the front of the house. That was C2, I think. Now, could the witness be asked where he was standing while he was watching the events he talked about. At what corner -- from what corner he was watching the scene --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whether he was in this street or lane --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: And when he spoke of a street or a road, did he mean this road going back to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Probably it's not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: Just to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Eser.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you understood the Court's question?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand it. As I said, the APC parked near the municipal building, and that's in the street leading to this private house, which is at the top of the street, looking from the municipal building. I was standing next to the APC, observing, because I was wounded, and I was trying to get into the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, let me clarify. From the spot where you were standing, were you able to see the entire street leading to this house?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to see the house or the corner of the house you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I could see it. But I couldn't see the entrance because the entrance was at the side of the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ESER
utterances.text: So basically what you see on the photo you could also see when you were standing in front of the municipal building. So we have a view, similar view as you have made on the photo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the house. I couldn't see the house from any other angle because I was standing next to the APC, near the municipal building. I don't know of any other house. This is the house where the UNPROFOR man went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in connection with this, another question: When this was going on, were there people in the street or was it empty?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Well, you could see the whole street. There weren't people there. There were no people between the APC and the house. The street was empty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as it's time for a break, maybe we can play the video after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I perfectly agree with you, Ms. Vidovic. So we'll have a 30-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we were going to see again part of the same video. Wait until the accused has got his -- it's okay. We can proceed now, Ms. Vidovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please play the video.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this still once again. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't see anything on your screen?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I can see the text only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, Usher -- you will be assisted by our usher. It's no problem. Then perhaps do you want him to see the previous -- or just this still that there is on the screen now, on the monitor now?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like the witness to identify the persons he mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take a look at this photograph and tell us who you know and who you had seen at the time.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: At the top left corner, there's Sahin Zahirovic in the white jacket; and I can see the person who's ill, wounded, who's being taken; and I can see the person in the blue jacket, who I don't know. I can also see a tall man in uniform who was beckoning to us to come to their assistance, to us who were standing by the APC. I don't know the man, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the person the arrow is pointing at?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. That's the man who came out of the house that was at the corner, who was not with the UNPROFOR. He was with a man who had one arm missing and was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Pause for the time being. We are, for the record, at 01.31, and the last person the witness refers to is standing to the right of a person wearing a -- what appears to be a purple jacket and a dark cap in the centre of the photograph. The person that is being carried by -- this person with the purple jacket and the -- and -- and the soldier -- what appears to be a soldier, with a blue cap, presumably an UNPROFOR soldier, the one in the middle, the injured or -- person, do you recognise the person? Do you know who he is? The one who was ultimately carried away and put on a stretcher?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the sick person who was taken out of that house. I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but you have -- you have no idea whether he was Bosnian, he was Serbian or Croat or any other kind of nationality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Yes, let's -- do you want to show more to the witness from this video or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In connection with this, Witness, did you take a good look at the person who was placed on the stretcher, the person His Honour was asking you about? Did you take a good look at him when he was laying on the stretcher whilst being taken into the APC?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him. He was very exhausted and very ill, as were all of us who were waiting there next to the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any visible injuries or bruises on his face?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have any bandages on him that you were able to see?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I was looking at the person carefully in order to see whether I'd recognise the person on the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you recognise him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. Nobody recognised him at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At one point I asked you whether the person had any sort of bandages on him that you were able to see.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. There were no bandages. I looked at the person quite carefully, the person on the stretcher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you remember what happened next, after the APC left?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I was watching closely when the man on the stretcher was being put on the APC. At one point I even got on to the APC, but the -- there was one soldier there who told me to get out. And then the man on the stretcher was put in and the door closed, the door of the APC, that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what happened next when the door of the APC was closed?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We were desperate because we were not the ones among those who were in the APC. We wanted to be evacuated. We started yelling at this tall man who we saw on the video wearing a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you addressing him in particular?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: We were under the impression that he was involved in what was going on. We didn't really know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this person a Bosnian Muslim or a foreigner?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he speak Bosnian when you addressed him, the tall man, I mean?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: He spoke Bosnian. All of us spoke Serbo-Croat. One could not distinguish who was who based on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You told us earlier that you saw the man without an arm who went in the direction of that house. Did there come a time that he showed up again after the APC left, or not?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. This person without an arm, wearing civilian clothes, who had come out of that house, came to us and told us that the APC had left for Zvornik and not for Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to this event, did you know this person who had one arm missing?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the APC left, did you get to know anything about this man?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. We took quite an interest in him because he was with the UNPROFOR men. We started yelling at him, telling him why we weren't able to be evacuated with the APC since we were wounded as well. The people who were close by addressed him by the name of Zele and told us that Zele was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this happened, were you able to see this one-armed policeman in Srebrenica again?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Two or three months later, I saw him in Srebrenica on several occasions. Everybody said that he was a policeman, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown a photograph, Defence exhibit. The photograph is part of the clip from D890.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the photograph. Do you recognise anyone shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's the man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe the man you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: This is the man without the arm. At the time I saw him, he did not have a uniform; he was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the man who was with the UNPROFOR men on that day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which of the three? Tell us, please.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: The one in the middle. At the time, his hair was longer and he had stubble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The beard you're mentioning, was it a long one or a short one?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: A short one. It was stubble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this photograph be assigned an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly, Ms. Vidovic. This will become Defence Exhibit D1011.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember whether you spent a longer period of time in front of the municipal building on that day?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said, I was standing in front of the municipal building from very early on in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after these events, did you stay there for a long time still?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Until the evening. We were standing there waiting for the APC to return in order for us to be evacuated as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we play the video-clip again and the part from 02.10 to 02.16. Please stop at 02.16.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please watch this part of the video closely and tell us whether you remember seeing on that day a car that was close to the scene of these events.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. The car that can be seen in the video. At 7.00 in the morning, when I came to the municipal building, the car was parked there throughout the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you remember this?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I remember this very well because my leg hurt and I was leaning against the car as I was waiting for the APC to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall what sort of car it was?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was dark blue - navy blue - or black. I'm not sure. I haven't noticed the make. It was a very dirty car indeed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you about another detail, if you remember. Was it a car with dark, tinted glass or did it have the normal sort of glass on the windows?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I remember that it wasn't dark tinted because I glanced into the interior of the car to see whether I'd find any food there. I was hungry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You've told us several times that you watched carefully what was going on around you. You also told us that you saw General Morillon. Do you remember if General Morillon was there when this particular person was put on the APC and taken to Zvornik? Was he present at the location where this happened at any time during the day?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. He wasn't there at any time. I was closely observing UNPROFOR men. They were very young, and General Morillon wasn't there on that day, on the day this event occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this particular place on that day, was there Naser Oric to be found in the vicinity of this person you called sick at any time?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. I was following what was happening closely, and I saw the sick man being brought over, placed on the stretcher, and into the APC. I saw the APC's door being closed. On that day Naser Oric was not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If Naser Oric had been there in the vicinity of this sick person, as you call him, would you have noticed him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, I would have noticed him. I was observing what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if someone were to assert that in front of the APC a black Mercedes or any other black vehicle arrived on that day and that Oric got out of that car and he himself personally handed that person over to the UNPROFOR men, on the basis of what you saw that day, would that be true?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. It wouldn't. What I said today is true because I was following what was going on. I was observing as the person was placed on the stretcher and put into the APC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, at any time prior to this event or after this event, did you see Naser Oric there or did any one of those present there mention him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No, nobody did. Nobody could say that he was there when I myself never mentioned his name. I myself was there and following everything closely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did UNPROFOR ever evacuate you?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell His Honours when it was that you left Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: In the month of July 1993, with a group of people. I set out for Tuzla on foot. People with me were from Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and Kamenica. On our way to Tuzla -- or rather, as we were going to Tuzla, many people got killed. At nightfall a large group set out for Tuzla. At a place near Han Pijesak they were ambushed and more than 80 people were killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people from your group managed to reach Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: About 30 or so people managed to get through. We were waylaid at several places along our way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many of you did head out for the journey?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Some 80 or so of us, whereas the other group was a bit larger.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Guster, my name is Di Fazio; I have a few questions for you. You met Mr. Oric in 1988. Where did you meet him?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. On my way to work from Cerska to Belgrade. We were on a bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before that or is that the first time you made his acquaintance?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: In 1988 and in 1989, when all of us worked together, we knew each other and would see each other. Other than that, we did not meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I understand, do I, correctly, that the first time you actually met Mr. Oric or were introduced to him, found out who he was, was on your way from Cerska to Belgrade. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I don't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's okay. I understand that. But it was in 1988, was it?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you continue to see him in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. We did not meet in Belgrade because we were doing different jobs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. So you had no contact with him in Belgrade while you were there up until the time you returned to Cerska, at around the time the war started?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So am I correct that you don't -- up until the war started, you only met Mr. Oric once. Is that correct or not? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. As I've said, that was in the period from 1988 to 1989. It was in that period that I saw him perhaps twice or three times. But I did not see him in Belgrade. We would meet on our journey there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I see. I understand you now. So you were working in Belgrade and you would come back home from time to time and you would see Mr. Oric on the bus as you were coming back. Now do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: From the people who introduced me to him from Cerska, they told me that he worked as a policeman in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know doing -- precisely what sort of job he was doing as a policeman in Belgrade? Do you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So would it be fair to say that by time war started he wasn't exactly a friend of yours or well-known to you; he was just a person who you'd met on a couple of occasions and had been introduced to. An acquaintance more than a friend. Would that be -- would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Well, yes. We knew each other only from those trips we made. We did not meet for coffee. It was only whilst we were travelling that we would meet each other, and that was how we got to know each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You saw a clip earlier on this morning. Madam Vidovic showed you a clip where you could see Mr. Oric in a crowd wearing a yellow -- a jacket with a yellow hood. At that point of time, your relationship with Mr. Oric was still the same, wasn't it? In other words, you were just acquaintances, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. I was among the large group of people, some 10 to 15 metres away, when at one point Naser Oric showed up wearing this yellow hood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you met him and spoken to him in 1992 in -- I'm thinking in particular of the period following the outbreak of war.

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what he was doing in the period of time between the outbreak of war in 1992 and that occasion when you saw him with the yellow hood?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. The people were preoccupied with saving their own skin. Nobody was interested in Naser Oric at the time. I didn't know who he was or what he was doing at the time. We were merely concerned with coming out alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a well-known figure in your village of Gusteri or in the villages of Cerska, Konjevic Polje, and other villages in your area? Was he a well-known figure?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard anything about his activities or conduct, what he was doing, during the war in 1992? You had no information about that at all. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This -- I just want to ask you some questions about this group that you -- that you mentioned in your -- in your village of Gusteri. It was a group of about 20 men, and you couldn't become part of it because you didn't have a weapon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I didn't have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Its leader was a gentleman named Meho Velic. Do you know how he became its leader?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I remember only that we got together, and someone said: There's a war breaking out. There are no weapons. People only had hunting rifles. That wasn't enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did that group stay the same in size and did that group keep the same weapons throughout 1992?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: Yes. Throughout 1992 they had the same weapons. As for the group, it got smaller and smaller because people got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it never increased in size, expanding, and it never acquired any further weapons, perhaps captured through fighting, that you're aware of anyway?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Velic, Meho Velic, was he ever answerable to anyone else other than the -- other than the people who were -- who composed the group?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No. It was the hamlet that this group with Meho Velic were defending. He didn't give any information to anybody.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know if the group ever cooperated with other groups in the area in fighting the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just to be clear, by that do you mean you have no idea, you have no knowledge, or are you saying that it never cooperated with other groups, other local village groups in the area, in fighting the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I wasn't part of the group, and I didn't find out what the group was doing because all I was doing was collecting food with other unarmed men who went with me to collect food for the refugees who were arriving in my hamlet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Right. Were you ever aware of this group of armed men from Gusteri go -- leaving the village and going off to fight in other areas around -- in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you go to Srebrenica at all in the period of time from the outbreak of war up until I think -- or let me rephrase that. When did you -- when did you actually go to Srebrenica and take up residence there, the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EJUB GUSTER
utterances.text: I didn't go to Srebrenica before the war, and I didn't know Srebrenica. It was only when the war broke out and when the Serbs, I might say, expelled us. That was when I went to Srebrenica, and I only stayed there briefly. This was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
